snapshot.stmt:
For a fixed short-term-outcome system and source-conditional law \(P\), let \(n=n_E+n_O\) and define the artificial superpopulation law \(P_n^{\circ}\) by
\[
 P_n^{\circ}(G=E)=\frac{n_E}{n},
 \qquad
 P_n^{\circ}(G=O)=\frac{n_O}{n},
 \qquad
 P_n^{\circ}(\cdot\mid G=g)=P(\cdot\mid G=g).
\]
Every norm in the statement below is \(\|\cdot\|_2=\|\cdot\|_{L_2(P_n^{\circ})}\).  Use a fixed number \(L_0\ge2\) of observational-only cross-fitting folds, independent i.i.d. observations within the two mutually independent sources, \(n_E,n_O\to\infty\), and \(n_E/n_O\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).  Suppose Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang Theorem~4 statements 1 and 2, their square-integrable latent outcome and selection bridge premises, the corresponding observed moment equations, and both parts of their Assumption~8 hold with nuisance limits equal to the true bridges \(h_0\) and \(q_0\).  Thus, for every \(1\le\ell\le L_0\),
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0(\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{h,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat h^{(-\ell)}-h_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{h,n}),
\]
\[
 \|\mathsf T_0^\star(\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0)\|_2=O_P(\delta_{q,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q^{(-\ell)}-q_0\|_2=O_P(\rho_{q,n}),
\]
all four rates tend to zero, and
\[
 \min\{\delta_{h,n}\rho_{q,n},\rho_{h,n}\delta_{q,n}\}
 =o(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Define the two score moments printed in their Theorem~5, kept distinct from this paper's arm-normalized \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\), by
\[
 V_E^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \left\{\frac{A-P(A=1\mid G=E)}{P(A=1\mid G=E)}
 \bigl(h_0(S_3,S_2,A,X)-\mu_0(A)\bigr)\right\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=E\right]
\]
and
\[
 V_O^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \left\{\frac{A-P(A=1\mid G=O)}{P(A=1\mid G=O)}
 q_0(S_2,S_1,A,X)
 \bigl(Y-h_0(S_3,S_2,A,X)\bigr)\right\}^2
 \mathrel{\Big|}G=O\right].
\]
If these two moments are finite and strictly positive, their Theorem~5 states that
\[
 \sqrt n\,(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DR}}-\tau_0)
 \rightsquigarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,
 \frac{1+\lambda}{\lambda}V_E^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 +(1+\lambda)V_O^{\mathrm{IKM}}\right).
\]
This cited statement records the source's printed normalization only.  It neither identifies \(V_g^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) with this paper's \(V_{g,d}\) nor supplies the arm-normalized fixed-path expansion used by the post-selection theorem.

lem:second-order-allocation-loss.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 Z_m=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}.
\]
By hypothesis, \(Z_m=O_P(r_{V,m})=o_P(1)\).  Finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) and the displayed uniform bounds furnish constants \(0<\nu_-<\nu_+<\infty\) containing every population variance and every cost.  On the event
\[
 \mathcal E_m=\{Z_m<\nu_-/2\}\cap\{\underline v_m<\nu_-/2\}, \tag{1}
\]
whose probability tends to one, every estimated variance is positive and exceeds \(\underline v_m\).  Hence the truncation in \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) is inactive.

For
\[
 A_d(x,y)=\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}}
 {\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}y}},
\]
the gradients are uniformly bounded on a common compact rectangle around all population pairs.  The mean-value theorem and (1) therefore yield
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|
 =O_P(r_{V,m}). \tag{2}
\]
The population optimal shares form a finite subset of \((0,1)\); hence there is \(a_0>0\) such that, with probability tending to one,
\[
 a_0\le\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\le1-a_0
 \qquad(d\in\mathcal D). \tag{3}
\]

For fixed \(d\), set \(a=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}\), \(b=c_{O,d}V_{O,d}\), and \(F_d(u)=a/u+b/(1-u)\).  The budget-profile theorem gives \(u_d^*=\alpha_d^*(P)=\sqrt a/(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)\) and \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2\).  A direct calculation gives the exact loss identity
\[
 F_d(u)-\mathcal V_d^*(P)
 =\mathcal V_d^*(P)\frac{(u-u_d^*)^2}{u(1-u)}. \tag{4}
\]
Combining (2)--(4), uniformly over the finite design family, gives
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}
 |F_d(\widehat\alpha_{d,m})-\mathcal V_d^*(P)|
 =O_P(r_{V,m}^2). \tag{5}
\]

On the event (3), both continuous source counts are at least a positive constant times \(B\).  For all sufficiently large \(B\), the floor inequality used in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) applies uniformly and gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 0\le{}&B\left\{
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
 \right\}-F_d(\widehat\alpha_{d,m})\\
 &\le\frac{C}{B}
\end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
with one finite constant \(C\) for all \(d\).  Equations (5)--(6) prove the asserted \(O_P(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1})\) bound.  The stipulated zero convention matters only off an event whose probability tends to zero, so it does not alter this stochastic order.  Equation (1) also shows that truncation is asymptotically inactive, which proves the final assertion.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\mathcal D\) be finite and nonempty. Suppose the costs and population variance components obey
\[
0<\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\min\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}
\le
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{c_{E,d},c_{O,d},V_{E,d},V_{O,d}\}<\infty.
\]
Suppose
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{
|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}=O_P(r_{V,m}),
\qquad r_{V,m}=o(1),
\qquad \underline v_m\downarrow0,
\]
and define \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}\) by the full-catalogue pilot selector. For every \(d\) inside the following maximum, assign the entire floor-count expression the value zero whenever either floor count is zero. Then, along every joint sequence \(m\to\infty\) and \(B\to\infty\),
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
=O_P\!\left(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1}\right).
\]
In particular, allocation estimation enters the profiled value only at second order, and the asymptotically inactive truncation contributes no term to the sharp rate.

defs.def:pilot-selector: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), fit the two observed bridge equations by cross-fitting on \(\mathcal P_m\), estimate \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) by foldwise score second moments, form \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}\widehat V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}\widehat V_{O,d}})^2\), select a deterministic-tie-broken \(\widehat d_m\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*\), compute \(\widehat\alpha_{d,m}=\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}/[\sqrt{c_{E,d}(\widehat V_{E,d}\vee\underline v_m)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}(\widehat V_{O,d}\vee\underline v_m)}]\), set \(\widehat\alpha_m=\widehat\alpha_{\widehat d_m,m}\), and purchase \(N_{E,B}=\lfloor\widehat\alpha_mB/c_{E,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) experimental units and \(N_{O,B}=\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_m)B/c_{O,\widehat d_m}\rfloor\) follow-up units.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.

assumptions.ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate: \(\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,|\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\}=O_P(r_{V,m})\), where probability is under the full-catalogue pilot law and the maximum is over the entire finite admissible family and both sources.
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

prop:postselection-wald-ate-corollary.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\).  By Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}identification\text{-}class}\),
\[
 \theta_d(P)=\tau\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathcal D.
\]
In particular, \(\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)=\tau\) for every pilot realization.  Therefore the studentized statistic in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}postselection\text{-}wald}\) is exactly
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)}{\widehat s_B}
\]
on \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), with the same zero extension on its complement.  The theorem's normal limit consequently gives the first conclusion.  Likewise, on \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\), its coverage event \(\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\) equals \(\{\tau\in I_B\}\); the complement of \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}}\) has probability tending to zero.  Hence the coverage conclusion of that theorem gives
\[
 P\{\tau\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), under the sampling and maintained estimator-level conditions of Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}postselection\text{-}wald}\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt B(\widehat\tau_B-\tau)}{\widehat s_B}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\tau\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta,
\]
with the same total-event zero extension as in that theorem.

defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]

lem:designwise-gradient.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), and abbreviate
\[
 H_d=(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X),\qquad L_d=(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X).
\]
Observed outcome-bridge existence gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\{Y-h_d(H_d)\mid L_d,G=O\}=0. \tag{1}
\]
Equivalently, \(T_dh_d=\mathbb E_P(Y\mid L_d,G=O)\).  Bijectivity of \(T_d\) makes this solution unique.  Thus \(h_d\), the two experimental means \(\mu_{d,a}\), and the contrast \(\theta_d(P)=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\) are identified from the two observed source laws.

Now take a bridge-differentiable regular two-source submodel in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), with source-conditional scores \(\ell_E,\ell_O\) and bridge derivative \(\dot h_d\).  Differentiability in quadratic mean, the declared \(L_2\) bridge differentiability, and the usual product rule give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \dot\mu_{d,a}
 &={\mathbb E}_P\!\left[
   \frac{\mathbf 1\{A=a\}}{p_{E,a}}
   \{h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},a,X)-\mu_{d,a}\}\ell_E
   \mathrel{\Big|}G=E\right]\\
 &\quad+{\mathbb E}_P\{\dot h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},a,X)\mid A=a,G=E\}. \tag{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
The selection-bridge equation states that \(T_d^\star q_d\) is the conditional density ratio of \((S_{3d},S_{2d},X)\) in source \(E\) relative to source \(O\), within each treatment arm.  Therefore, for every square-integrable \(f(H_d)\), iterated expectation gives
\[
 {\mathbb E}_P\{f(H_d)\mid A=a,G=E\}
 ={\mathbb E}_P\{q_d(L_d)f(H_d)\mid A=a,G=O\}. \tag{3}
\]

The defining submodel condition permits differentiation of (1) in conditional \(L_2\).  The conditional-score centering term is multiplied by the zero conditional residual mean in (1), and hence
\[
 T_d\dot h_d
 ={\mathbb E}_P[\{Y-h_d(H_d)\}\ell_O\mid L_d,G=O]. \tag{4}
\]
Apply (3) with \(f=\dot h_d\), then apply (4) and iterated expectation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 {\mathbb E}_P(\dot h_d\mid A=a,G=E)
 &={\mathbb E}_P(q_d\dot h_d\mid A=a,G=O)\\
 &={\mathbb E}_P[q_d\{Y-h_d(H_d)\}\ell_O\mid A=a,G=O]. \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting (2) at \(a=0\) from (2) at \(a=1\), substituting (5), and using source-arm positivity to express arm-conditional expectations as source-conditional inner products yields
\[
 \dot\theta_d(P)
 ={\mathbb E}_P(\phi_{E,d}\ell_E\mid G=E)
  +{\mathbb E}_P(\phi_{O,d}\ell_O\mid G=O). \tag{6}
\]
The definitions of \(\mu_{d,a}\) imply \({\mathbb E}_P(\phi_{E,d}\mid G=E)=0\), while (1) implies \({\mathbb E}_P(\phi_{O,d}\mid G=O)=0\).  The nondegenerate-component condition makes both components square-integrable.  Thus they are the two source components of a pathwise gradient on the declared submodel class.  For independent source samples of sizes \(n_E,n_O\), the variances of their sample averages add, giving
\[
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}. \tag{7}
\]
This derivation uses the explicit bridge-differentiability restriction at the differentiation step (4); it does not infer local inverse stability from pointwise bijectivity.  The identification part and the definitions of the source-score variances remain meaningful without that path restriction.  No latent causal restriction, completeness condition, or equality with \(\tau\) was used.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), the observed-data bridge contrast \(\theta_d(P):=\mu_{d,1}-\mu_{d,0}\) is identified. Along every bridge-differentiable regular two-source submodel for design \(d\) at \(P\) in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), its pathwise gradient has source components \(\phi_{E,d}\) and \(\phi_{O,d}\). Hence independent source sample sizes \(n_E,n_O\) have source-score variance
\[
 \frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O},
\]
and this is the gradient variance on the declared bridge-differentiable submodel class. Outside that class, \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) remain source-score variances, but pointwise bijectivity alone does not assert pathwise differentiability. No latent causal restriction, completeness condition, or equality with \(\tau\) is used or asserted.

defs.def:bridge-differentiable-submodel:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), and write
\[
 H_d=(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X),\qquad L_d=(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X).
\]
A regular two-source parametric submodel \(\{P_t:|t|<t_0\}\) through \(P=P_0\), with source-conditional scores \(\ell_E\) and \(\ell_O\), is called \emph{bridge-differentiable for design \(d\) at \(P\)} when the following conditions hold.  First, the source-conditional laws are dominated on a common support and the path is differentiable in quadratic mean in each source.  Second, for all sufficiently small \(|t|\), \(P_t\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and its design-\(d\) outcome bridge \(h_{d,t}\) is unique.  Third, after identifying the common \(L_2\) coordinate spaces along the dominated path, there is \(\dot h_d\in L_2(H_d\mid G=O)\) such that
\[
 \left\|\frac{h_{d,t}-h_{d,0}}{t}-\dot h_d\right\|_{L_2(P(\cdot\mid G=O))}\longrightarrow0,
\]
and the conditional bridge equation
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_t}\{Y-h_{d,t}(H_d)\mid L_d,G=O\}=0
\]
may be differentiated at \(t=0\) in \(L_2(L_d\mid G=O)\) using the conditional-score rule.  This is a restriction on submodels, not a consequence of pointwise bijectivity of \(T_d\).

assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

thm:budget-profile.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), and set
\[
 x_E=\frac{\alpha B}{c_{E,d}},\qquad
 x_O=\frac{(1-\alpha)B}{c_{O,d}}.
\]
The asserted lower bound on \(B\) makes \(x_E,x_O\ge2\). For every \(x\ge2\),
\[
 0\le \frac1{\lfloor x\rfloor}-\frac1x
 =\frac{x-\lfloor x\rfloor}{x\lfloor x\rfloor}
 \le\frac2{x^2}, \tag{1}
\]
because \(0\le x-\lfloor x\rfloor<1\) and \(\lfloor x\rfloor\ge x/2\). Applying (1) to the two source counts gives the exact decomposition
\[
 B\left\{\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)}\right\}
 =\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)
\]
and
\[
 0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)
 \le\frac2B\left\{
 \frac{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2}{\alpha^2}
 +\frac{V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2}{(1-\alpha)^2}\right\}. \tag{2}
\]
For fixed \(d\) and \(\alpha\), the right-hand side tends to zero. The left-hand side is the budget-scaled source-score variance; by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}designwise\text{-}gradient}\), it is also the budget-scaled gradient variance along every bridge-differentiable submodel.

Put \(a_d=c_{E,d}V_{E,d}\) and \(b_d=c_{O,d}V_{O,d}\). Positive costs and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\) imply \(a_d,b_d>0\). Direct algebra gives
\[
 \frac{a_d}{\alpha}+\frac{b_d}{1-\alpha}
 -(\sqrt{a_d}+\sqrt{b_d})^2
 =\frac{\{(1-\alpha)\sqrt{a_d}-\alpha\sqrt{b_d}\}^2}
 {\alpha(1-\alpha)}\ge0. \tag{3}
\]
Equality holds exactly when
\[
 \alpha=\frac{\sqrt{a_d}}{\sqrt{a_d}+\sqrt{b_d}}
 =\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}}
 {\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}}
 =\alpha_d^*(P).
\]
This proves uniqueness and
\[
 \mathcal V_d^*(P)
 =(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}})^2.
\]
On \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), the observed contrast equals the common causal target, but the gradient interpretation still requires the declared bridge-differentiable submodel restriction. If that gradient is additionally canonical for \(\tau\), its variance is the local semiparametric efficiency lower bound; the separately recorded fixed-system Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang result supplies that interpretation under its own normalization and premises. Thus the calculation itself is a cost profile of source-score variance and does not, by algebra alone, assert a new cross-design canonical-efficiency theorem.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), as \(B\to\infty\),
\[
B\left\{\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_{E,B}(d,\alpha)}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_{O,B}(d,\alpha)}\right\}
=\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)+\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P),
\]
where, once \(B\ge2\max\{c_{E,d}/\alpha,c_{O,d}/(1-\alpha)\}\),
\[
0\le\mathfrak r_{d,B}(\alpha;P)\le \frac2B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}c_{E,d}^2}{\alpha^2}+
\frac{V_{O,d}c_{O,d}^2}{(1-\alpha)^2}\right\}.
\]
Thus the floor-count source-score variance converges to \(\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\). The unique minimizer and minimum are
\[
\alpha_d^*(P)=\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}}{\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}},
\qquad
\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\left(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}\right)^2.
\]
On the bridge-differentiable submodel class of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), this profiles the designwise gradient variance. For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), it profiles the gradient variance of the common causal target only on that declared submodel class. It is a local causal semiparametric efficiency bound only when the designwise gradient is additionally canonical for \(\tau\), in particular under the fixed-system Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang conditions recorded separately.

\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).

thm:pilot-oracle-regret.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Write
\[
 v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P),\qquad
 \widehat v_d=\widehat{\mathcal V}_{d,m}^*,
 \qquad v_*=\min_{d\in\mathcal D}v_d,
\]
and choose \(d^*\in D^*(P)\).  By the definition of \(\varepsilon_m\) and the minimizing property of \(\widehat d_m\),
\[
 v_{\widehat d_m}
 \le \widehat v_{\widehat d_m}+\varepsilon_m
 \le \widehat v_{d^*}+\varepsilon_m
 \le v_*+2\varepsilon_m. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(v_*\le v_{\widehat d_m}\),
\[
 0\le v_{\widehat d_m}-v_*\le2\varepsilon_m. \tag{2}
\]
If \(\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\), the definition of \(\gamma(P)\) gives
\[
 \gamma(P)\le v_{\widehat d_m}-v_*\le2\varepsilon_m. \tag{3}
\]
When every design is optimal, the left event is empty; otherwise finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) gives \(\gamma(P)>0\).

Set
\[
 Z_m=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\max\bigl\{|\widehat V_{E,d}-V_{E,d}|,
 |\widehat V_{O,d}-V_{O,d}|\bigr\}.
\]
The maintained pilot variance condition and its vanishing-rate companion give \(Z_m=O_P(r_{V,m})=o_P(1)\).  By the pilot construction and Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\),
\[
 \widehat v_d=G_d(\widehat V_{E,d},\widehat V_{O,d}),
 \qquad v_d=G_d(V_{E,d},V_{O,d}),
\]
where \(G_d(x,y)=(\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}y})^2\).  Positive population variances, positive costs, and finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) put all population pairs in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)^2\); with probability tending to one, the estimated pairs lie in a slightly larger such compact set.  The finitely many gradients \(\nabla G_d\) are uniformly bounded there.  Thus
\[
 \varepsilon_m=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat v_d-v_d|
 =O_P(r_{V,m})=o_P(1). \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) imply \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\to0\).

The same compact-set argument applied to
\[
 A_d(x,y)=\frac{\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}}
 {\sqrt{c_{E,d}x}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}y}}
\]
shows that the variance truncation is inactive with probability tending to one and
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|
 =O_P(r_{V,m}). \tag{5}
\]
Finally, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}second\text{-}order\text{-}allocation\text{-}loss}\), whose premises are exactly the same maintained pilot variance condition, its vanishing rate, nondegeneracy, and the pilot definition, gives
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
=O_P(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1})=o_P(1).
\]
The deterministic tie rule was used only to choose an empirical minimizer in (1); the conclusion is therefore membership in the complete optimizer set, not convergence to an arbitrarily selected population minimizer.  Every stochastic conclusion in the proof is conditional on the maintained pilot variance condition; no primitive bridge learner or variance-rate derivation has been supplied.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). For the independently funded full-catalogue pilot selector,
\[
0\le\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)-\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\le2\varepsilon_m,
\qquad
\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\subseteq\{2\varepsilon_m\ge\gamma(P)\}.
\]
Conditional on the maintained full-catalogue pilot variance condition in Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}pilot\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), together with \(r_{V,m}=o(1)\) from Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}pilot\text{-}variance\text{-}rate\text{-}vanishes}\) and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\),
\[
\varepsilon_m=O_P(r_{V,m}),
\qquad
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}|\widehat\alpha_{d,m}-\alpha_d^*(P)|=O_P(r_{V,m}),
\]
and \(P\{\widehat d_m\notin D^*(P)\}\to0\), with the event empty when \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\). With the stipulated zero value when either floor count vanishes,
\[
\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left|B\left\{
\frac{V_{E,d}}{\lfloor\widehat\alpha_{d,m}B/c_{E,d}\rfloor}
+\frac{V_{O,d}}{\lfloor(1-\widehat\alpha_{d,m})B/c_{O,d}\rfloor}
\right\}-\mathcal V_d^*(P)\right|
=O_P(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1})=o_P(1).
\]
The selector consistently chooses the complete optimizer set under these maintained pilot conditions; no causal interpretation is needed for this observable bridge-functional regret statement. The theorem does not derive the maintained variance condition from a primitive bridge learner.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Conditional on the independent full-catalogue pilot, suppose the purchased experimental and observational samples are mutually independent and independent and identically distributed within source. Use the selected-design-only estimator, score moments, total event, variance estimator, statistic, and interval of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}selected\text{-}wald\text{-}variance}\). Impose the maintained estimator-level conditions in Assumptions~\(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}outcome\text{-}weak\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}outcome\text{-}strong\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}selection\text{-}weak\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}selection\text{-}strong\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}bridge\text{-}product\text{-}rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}postselection\text{-}multiplier\text{-}condition}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}pilot\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}main\text{-}gradient\text{-}variance\text{-}rate}\), together with the four declared bridge-rate vanishing conditions and the pilot and main-study variance-rate vanishing conditions. Let \(m\to\infty\), \(B\to\infty\), and \(\underline v_m=o(1)\). Then
\[
 P(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{tot}})\longrightarrow1,
\]
\[
 s_{0,B}^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \widehat s_B^2-\mathcal V_{\widehat d_m}^*(P)=o_P(1),
\]
and the selected observable contrast obeys
\[

 \frac{\sqrt B\{\widehat\tau_B-\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\}}{\widehat s_B}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 P\{\theta_{\widehat d_m}(P)\in I_B\}\longrightarrow1-\eta.
\]
All listed nuisance-rate, product-rate, multiplier, pilot-variance, and main-study-variance requirements are sufficient conditions of this conditional theorem. They are not conclusions of the observable law class or of the cited fixed-design theory. Primitive selected-path attainability without additional learner structure remains the separate open object \(\mathrm{oeq{:}primitive\text{-}selected\text{-}path\text{-}attainability}\).

For every deterministic sequence \(d_B\in\mathcal D\), \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\) with \(|\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\to0\), and fixed \(L\),
\[
\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_{d_B}\|_{2,O,q,d_B}=O_P(\rho_{q,B}).
\]
assumptions.ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate:
For every deterministic sequence \(d_B\in\mathcal D\), \(\alpha_B\in(0,1)\) with \(|\alpha_B-\alpha_{d_B}^*(P)|\to0\), and fixed \(L\),
\[
\max_{1\le\ell\le L}\|T_{d_B}^{\star}(\widehat q_{d_B,B}^{(-\ell)}-q_{d_B})\|_{2,B}^{\circ}=O_P(\delta_{q,B}).
\]

prop:anchor-reduction.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and the singleton design \(d\).  Put
\[
 \alpha=\frac{c_{E,d}n_E}{B}.
\]
Because \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\) and both counts and costs are positive,
\[
 0<\alpha<1,
 \qquad
 1-\alpha=\frac{c_{O,d}n_O}{B}.
\]
Substitution into the design-value profile gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac1B\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)
 &=\frac1B\left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{c_{E,d}n_E/B}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{c_{O,d}n_O/B}\right\}\\
 &=\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}.
\end{aligned}
\]
By Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}designwise\text{-}gradient}\), the last expression is the fixed-system two-source pathwise-gradient variance for \(\theta_d(P)\).  If \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\), the causal-identification premise gives \(\theta_d(P)=\tau\).  Under the additional fixed-system canonical-gradient premises, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) identifies the corresponding two-source canonical-gradient variance as the causal semiparametric efficiency lower bound.  Without those causal-identification and canonical-gradient premises, the displayed equality remains only the observable bridge-functional identity.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), if \(\mathcal D=\{d\}\), the main study fixes positive counts \(n_E,n_O\), and \(B=c_{E,d}n_E+c_{O,d}n_O\), then
\[
 \frac1B\mathcal V_d\!\left(\frac{c_{E,d}n_E}{B};P\right)
 =\frac{V_{E,d}}{n_E}+\frac{V_{O,d}}{n_O}.
\]
The right-hand side is the fixed-system two-source pathwise-gradient variance for \(\theta_d(P)\). If \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}\) and the fixed-system Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang canonical-gradient conditions hold, it is also their causal semiparametric efficiency bound for \(\tau\); absent those additional conditions only the observable bridge-functional identity is asserted.

defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

thm:predictive-impossibility.proof_tex:
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) proves every center assertion: membership in both law classes, common identification, the continuous CLW ordering, the two bridge-profile orderings, the source-score values, equality of the named center ratios, their fixed-\(\chi\) expansion, and the optimized sharp elbow.  In particular, its floor calculation proves more than the stated eventual claim:
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\{d_{\mathrm p}\}
 \quad\text{for every }B\ge5\chi,
\]
so one may take \(B_0(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=5\chi\).  At a center balanced treatment gives
\[
 V_{g,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{g,d},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon}),
 \qquad g\in\{E,O\},                                    \tag{37}
\]
which proves (3)--(4).  The exact center ratio from the sharp-elbow lemma expands as
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}),
\]
and its rescaled optimization proves (6)--(7).

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\) proves that regularity, CLW admissibility, common identification, the named ordering, and the arm-normalized bridge ordering persist in each constrained-model ball used to define \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\).  Every center lies in its ball, and the ratio on the corresponding ball exceeds one half of a center ratio that is larger than \((\epsilon^{-2}+14)/726\).  Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves (8).  The same lemma proves the stated law-specific eventual integer conclusion.

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\) preserves the strict IKM optimizer and more than one half of the diverging center IKM ratio.  Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}region}\) intersects that radius with the preceding stability radius, proving (9).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}ikmw\text{-}fixed\text{-}system\text{-}efficiency}\) supplies the absolute causal-efficiency interpretation only under its additional fixed-system premises.

At a center, the sharp-elbow lemma separately proves equality of the affine CLW residual and the unrestricted raw risk.  It follows that the raw-risk selector is \(\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\) and that its arm-normalized and IKM ratios equal the named ratios, without making any off-center substitution.

Finally, the primitive costs obey
\[
 c_1+c_2=\kappa,
 \qquad c_3+c_4=1<\kappa,
 \qquad C_{d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi,
 \qquad C_{d_{\mathrm e}}=5,
\]
and their two sourcewise gaps equal \(5(\chi-1)/2>0\).  Thus the center primitive cost vector lies in \(\mathcal C_\kappa\) and has paired-cost ratio \(\chi\).  On the relative cap-feasible cost manifold, primitive costs, the two affine criteria, and both bridge profiles are continuous.  Their center gaps are strict.  Consequently a sufficiently small relative cost neighborhood preserves the strict sourcewise cost ordering, the named objective ordering, and both bridge-profile orderings for sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\).  No step invokes the empirical least-squares rule, OGA, an arbitrary predictive method, or a bridge-role assignment by the comparator paper.

snapshot.stmt:
For the transported Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm population affine-linear measurement rule, the following impossibility holds. Fix \(B>0\). For every prescribed finite paired-cost disadvantage \(\chi>1\), every center \(P_{\chi,\epsilon}\), \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), belongs to \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\cap\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\), both bridge contrasts equal \(\tau=0\), and the named continuous selector chooses \(d_{\mathrm p}\) whereas both the arm-normalized and IKM-normalized bridge profiles choose \(d_{\mathrm e}\):
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad
 D^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})=D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\{d_{\mathrm e}\}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
The paired costs are \(5\chi\) and \(5\), and
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\frac32\frac{1-\epsilon^2}{1-\epsilon^2y_\chi^2}
 <\frac32<3
 =B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B). \tag{2}
\]
For each center there is a finite \(B_0(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\) such that the exact integer-budget selector also equals \(\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\) for every \(B\ge B_0(P_{\chi,\epsilon})\). Moreover,
\[
 V_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}
 =\frac{64}{75(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}+O_\chi(1),
 \qquad
 V_{E,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{E,d},
 \qquad
 V_{O,d}^{\mathrm{IKM}}=\frac14V_{O,d},                    \tag{3}
\]
\[
 \mathcal V_{d,\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon})
 =\frac14\mathcal V_d^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon}),               \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\frac{5\chi+1}{363(10\chi-3)}\epsilon^{-2}
 +O_\chi(\epsilon^{-1}).                                  \tag{5}
\]
Across the center family, any minimizing paired-cost factor satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)
 \sim \frac{\sqrt[3]{18}}{15}\epsilon^{-2/3},             \tag{6}
\]
and, for either named center ratio \(\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}\),
\[
 \epsilon^2\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\frac1{726}+\frac{5\sqrt[3]{12}}{968}\epsilon^{2/3}
 +o(\epsilon^{2/3}).                                       \tag{7}
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\) remains regular, CLW-admissible, and common-identifying, satisfies
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad D^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}}\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)=\infty, \tag{8}
\]
and has the law-specific eventual integer-selector conclusion. On \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}\),
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P;B)=\infty.          \tag{9}
\]
At every center the unrestricted raw-risk selector also chooses \(d_{\mathrm p}\), and its arm-normalized and IKM ratios equal the two named ratios; the generic open-region conclusions remain secondary. For each fixed \(\chi>1\), the center primitive cost vector lies in \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), has paired-cost ratio \(\chi\), and has a relatively open cost-manifold neighborhood preserving the strict cost and objective orderings for sufficiently small positive \(\epsilon\).

The obstruction concerns only the transported CLW population affine-linear residual-variance-over-sample-size rule with support mapped to \(M_d\). It does not refute Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm's randomized-trial theorem, their empirical equation~(3.6), their OGA procedure, an arbitrary predictive method, or a bridge-role assignment by that paper. The IKM profile has its absolute causal-efficiency interpretation only under the separately cited fixed-system premises.

defs.def:binary-ikmw-region:
Fix \(\chi>1\).  For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), jointly decrease \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) as permitted by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}exact\text{-}integer\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\).  Let \(\delta_\epsilon\) be the radius in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}region}\), choose
\[
 0<\widetilde\delta_\epsilon
 <\min\{\delta_\epsilon,r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\},
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi):
 \|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\widetilde\delta_\epsilon\right\}. \tag{1}
\]
The radii retain the conclusions used to define \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), together with the strict IKM optimizer ordering and the exact-integer IKM-ratio stability from Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}exact\text{-}integer\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\).  This is a relatively open subset of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\).
defs.def:binary-witness:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant, and take the nonredundant affine encoding \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\) to be zero-dimensional. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(C_{d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi\) and \(C_{d_{\mathrm e}}=5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and define the exact center residual function
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.                  \tag{1}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\), rather than this construction, proves that the unrestricted unadjusted risk and the distinct CLW affine-linear residual both equal (1) at the symmetric centers. No such equality is imposed on perturbations in the constrained model. The named transported CLW selector compares \(C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)/B\); the two generic unrestricted-risk selectors remain separate secondary comparisons.

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\), zero-dimensional \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\), constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j).                               \tag{2}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_{\epsilon}=P_{\chi,\epsilon}\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (2).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, full short-term external validity, source support, the sequential-outcome restriction, and both proxy-completeness conditions for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), define the two generic unrestricted observational prediction risks
\[
 R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}
 \mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O],
\]
\[
 R_d^A(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(A,X,Z_{M_d})}
 \mathbb E_P[(Y-f(A,X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O].                \tag{1}
\]
Their tie-preserving population selectors and arm-normalized source-score ratios are
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d(P),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d^A(P),
\]
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.           \tag{2}
\]
Distinctly, on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\), the transported Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm population rule uses the affine-linear residual variance \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\), not either unrestricted risk.  Under \(c(M_d,n)=nC_d\), its continuous and integer criteria, selectors, and arm-normalized ratio are those in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\):
\[
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{B},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)
 =\frac{r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor}.      \tag{3}
\]
The support is mapped only to \(M_d\), and this note's role assignment remains preattached.  No equality between \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\) and \(R_d(P)\) or \(R_d^A(P)\) is imposed away from the binary centers where it is proved.  The two unrestricted-risk rules in (1)--(2) are secondary comparisons and are not attributed to a named published proxy-selection workflow.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.
defs.def:clw-linear-cost-selector:
Fix the source-faithful transported comparison from Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\): treatment is completely randomized with equal arm allocation, and the two arms have the same affine-regression residual variance.  These are restrictions on the transported comparison, not on the persistent-confounding bridge law.  Map the published support \(\mathcal I(\gamma)\) only to \(M_d\); the role assignment \(r_d\) remains preattached by this note.

Choose a finite-dimensional nonredundant affine encoding \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\), with constant and reference columns removed, and define
\[
 \xi_d=(1,X_{\mathrm{nr}}^\top,Z_{M_d}^\top)^\top,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_d\xi_d^\top\mid G=O),
 \qquad
 g_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_dY\mid G=O).                       \tag{1}
\]
The domain \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\) consists of laws \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) such that, for every \(d\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Y^2+\|\xi_d\|^2\mid G=O)<\infty,
 \qquad \det\Gamma_d(P)\ne0,                              \tag{2}
\]
and the transported balanced comparison has the arm-homoskedastic residual required by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\).  The determinant condition concerns the full Gram matrix on the nonredundant basis; no pseudoinverse is used.  Put
\[
 \beta_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)=\Gamma_d(P)^{-1}g_d(P),
 \qquad
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)=
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \{Y-\xi_d^\top\beta_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\}^2\mid G=O
 \right].                                                   \tag{3}
\]
Under the linear paired-unit cost
\[
 c(M_d,n)=nC_d,
 \qquad C_d=c_{E,d}+c_{O,d},                                \tag{4}
\]
define the continuous and exact integer criteria by
\[
 n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=\frac{B}{C_d},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{B}, \tag{5}
\]
\[
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \begin{cases}
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)/\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor>0,\\
 +\infty,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor=0.
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{6}
\]
Retain all ties in
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B). \tag{7}
\]
The continuous and exact-integer arm-normalized best-tie ratios are
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.             \tag{8}
\]
The IKM-normalized continuous and integer ratios are defined in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\).  Equations (3)--(8) transport only the population affine-linear criterion.  The exact finite-catalogue empirical affine least-squares counterpart of equation~(3.6) is defined separately in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}empirical\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\).  Nothing here attributes persistent-confounding analysis, sequential bridge-role choice, or bridge-value results to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm, and no claim concerns their approximate OGA procedure or their original randomized-trial theorem.
defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

thm:sharp-predictive-operator-certificat.proof_tex:
\emph{Proof.}
Write \(p_d=R_d(P)\) and \(v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P)\).  The family \(\mathcal D\) is finite and nonempty.  Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}predictive\text{-}benchmark}\) gives \(0\le p_d<\infty\).  By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}components}\), the costs are positive and \(0<V_{E,d},V_{O,d}<\infty\).  The profile formula in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}budget\text{-}profile}\) therefore gives
\[
 0<v_d=
 \left(\sqrt{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}+
       \sqrt{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}\right)^2<\infty .             \tag{10}
\]
These are the support and boundary facts needed below: all denominators involving \(v_d\) are strictly positive, every displayed finite-set minimum or maximum is attained, and \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) is nonempty.

The order set \(\mathcal O_P\) is finite and nonempty because it contains every diagonal pair \((d,d)\).  Every ratio \(v_d/v_{d'}\) on it is positive and finite, while each diagonal ratio is one.  Thus
\[
 1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty .                         \tag{11}
\]
For \(C\ge0\), the implication in equation~\((2)\) holds for all \(d,d'\) exactly when
\[
 \frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}\le C
 \quad\text{for every }(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P,             \tag{12}
\]
where division is legitimate by equation~\((10)\).  Since the index set in equation~\((12)\) is finite, equation~\((12)\) is equivalent to \(C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\le C\).  This proves equations~\((1)\)--\((2)\) and the claimed sharpness of the pairwise constant.

Let \(d_{\mathrm{sel}}\) minimize \(v_d\) over \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\), and let \(d_*\) minimize \(v_d\) over \(\mathcal D\).  The best-tie selector has the exact multiplicative loss
\[
 \frac{v_{d_{\mathrm{sel}}}}{v_{d_*}}
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
        {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P).                                \tag{13}
\]
Consequently the least \(C\) bounding the selected value by \(C\min_{d'}v_{d'}\) is the ratio in equation~\((13)\) itself.  Since \(d_*\) is globally optimal, this ratio is at least one.  Since \(d_{\mathrm{sel}}\) minimizes prediction risk whereas \(d_*\) is merely an admissible design,
\[
 p_{d_{\mathrm{sel}}}\le p_{d_*};
\]
hence \((d_{\mathrm{sel}},d_*)\in\mathcal O_P\), and
\[
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)=\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)
 =\frac{v_{d_{\mathrm{sel}}}}{v_{d_*}}
 \le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P).                                 \tag{14}
\]
Together with equation~\((11)\), this proves equation~\((3)\).

Now let \(\mathcal Q\) be nonempty.  If one finite constant works for the best-tie rule at every \(P\in\mathcal Q\), equation~\((13)\) shows that the supremum of \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\) over \(\mathcal Q\) is bounded by that constant.  Conversely, if that supremum is finite, choosing it as \(C\) gives the uniform bound.  The identical argument using the exact equivalence in equation~\((12)\) proves the pairwise assertion with \(C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\).  This establishes the two uniform if-and-only-if statements.  It also shows why \(C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\), which uses only the realized prediction ordering and realized values, is the weakest exact lawwise pairwise comparison.  The operators \(T_d\) affect those realized values through the design-specific bridges, but finiteness in equation~\((11)\) needs no comparison between different operators.

We next prove the quadratic-form certificate.  For any numerical realization specified in the theorem, put
\[
 r_d(x)=\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)},
 \qquad x\in\mathcal X_d(P).                              \tag{15}
\]
The denominator is strictly positive by the stipulated positivity of \(Q_{R,d}\) on the nonzero cone.  By the definitions in equation~\((6)\), \(\Lambda_-(P)\) is the greatest constant \(L\) such that
\[
 LQ_{R,d}(x)\le F_d(x)
 \quad\text{for every }d\in\mathcal D,
 \ x\in\mathcal X_d(P),                                  \tag{16}
\]
and \(\Lambda_+(P)\) is the least constant \(U\) such that
\[
 F_d(x)\le UQ_{R,d}(x)
 \quad\text{for every }d\in\mathcal D,
 \ x\in\mathcal X_d(P).                                  \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, equations~\((16)\)--\((17)\) are respectively equivalent to \(L\le\inf_xr_d(x)\) for every \(d\), and to \(U\ge\sup_xr_d(x)\) for every \(d\).  Thus a strictly positive finite two-sided envelope exists if and only if
\[
 0<\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)<\infty,                   \tag{18}
\]
and the two endpoints in equation~\((18)\) are its sharp global lower and upper coefficients on the chosen cones.  This proves the asserted ``weakest envelope'' characterization.

Apply equations~\((16)\)--\((17)\) to the transported directions \(x_d(P)\).  Equations~\((4)\) and~\((18)\) yield, for every \(d\),
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)p_d\le v_d\le\Lambda_+(P)p_d.               \tag{19}
\]
In particular, equation~\((19)\) also forces every \(p_d\) in this numerical realization to be positive.  If \((d,d')\in\mathcal O_P\), then
\[
 \frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}
 \le
 \frac{\Lambda_+(P)p_d}{\Lambda_-(P)p_{d'}}
 \le \frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}.                  \tag{20}
\]
Taking the maximum over \(\mathcal O_P\), and combining the result with equation~\((14)\), proves equation~\((8)\).

It remains to justify the profiling and eigenvalue assertions.  For fixed \(d\) and \(x\), set
\[
 a=c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x),\qquad b=c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x),
\]
so \(a,b\ge0\).  For every \(0<\alpha<1\), direct expansion gives
\[
 \frac a\alpha+\frac b{1-\alpha}-(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2
 =\frac{\{(1-\alpha)\sqrt a-\alpha\sqrt b\}^2}
        {\alpha(1-\alpha)}\ge0.                           \tag{21}
\]
If \(a,b>0\), equality occurs at
\(
 \alpha=\sqrt a/(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)
\).
If \(a=0<b\), or \(b=0<a\), the lower bound is approached as \(\alpha\downarrow0\), or \(\alpha\uparrow1\), respectively; if \(a=b=0\), equality holds for every \(\alpha\).  Taking the infimum in equation~\((21)\) proves equation~\((9)\) in every boundary case.

The profiled map need not itself be quadratic.  For example, on \(\mathbb R^2\), take unit costs,
\[
 Q_E(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2,
 \qquad Q_O(x_1,x_2)=x_2^2.
\]
Then
\[
 F(x_1,x_2)=(|x_1|+|x_2|)^2.
\]
For the coordinate vectors \(e_1,e_2\),
\[
 F(e_1+e_2)+F(e_1-e_2)=8
 \ne4=2F(e_1)+2F(e_2),                                   \tag{22}
\]
contradicting the parallelogram identity satisfied by every quadratic form.  Thus a generalized-eigenvalue representation is unavailable in general.

Even in the finite-dimensional full-space case, at a fixed \(\alpha\) the quadratic numerator
\[
 G_{d,\alpha}(x)=
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}\alpha+
 \frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}
\]
satisfies \(F_d(x)\le G_{d,\alpha}(x)\) by equation~\((9)\).  Hence the largest generalized Rayleigh quotient of \(G_{d,\alpha}\) relative to positive-definite \(Q_{R,d}\) supplies an upper full-space envelope only.  It supplies neither the strictly positive lower coefficient in equation~\((16)\) nor equality in the two successive inequalities of equation~\((20)\).  Equality in equation~\((20)\) requires a law-realized ordered pair whose numerator direction attains \(\Lambda_+(P)\), whose denominator direction attains \(\Lambda_-(P)\), and whose prediction risks saturate the ordering.  Comparing such directions by one eigenproblem also requires placing the design-specific forms on a common space and normalizing by the positive lower envelope.  Bijectivity of each \(T_d\) gives none of these cross-design metric or attainment properties, and the scalar ordering \(p_d\le p_{d'}\) gives none either.  This proves the final assertions. \(\square\)

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_d=R_d(P),
 \qquad v_d=\mathcal V_d^*(P).
\]
Define the raw-prediction-order relation and its order-restricted design-value constant by
\[
 \mathcal O_P=\{(d,d')\in\mathcal D^2:p_d\le p_{d'}\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)=\max_{(d,d')\in\mathcal O_P}\frac{v_d}{v_{d'}}. \tag{1}
\]
Then \(1\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\), and, for every \(C\ge0\),
\[
 \bigl[p_d\le p_{d'}\Longrightarrow v_d\le C v_{d'}
 \text{ for all }d,d'\in\mathcal D\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C\ge C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P). \tag{2}
\]
The smallest constant for the actual best-tie raw prediction-risk rule is
\[
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)
 =\frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}v_d}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}v_{d'}}
 =\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P),
 \qquad
 1\le C_{\mathrm{sel}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty. \tag{3}
\]
Consequently, for any nonempty subclass \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), a finite constant uniform over \(\mathcal Q\) exists for the best-tie rule if and only if \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)<\infty\); for all pairwise raw-risk-order implications it exists if and only if \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)<\infty\). Thus (1), rather than an operator norm, is the weakest exact lawwise comparison for selection by raw population prediction risk. The design-specific operators \(T_d\) enter (1) through the bridges and hence through \(v_d\), but no further comparison of the operators is necessary for lawwise finiteness.

More specifically, consider any numerical realization of the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) with the following properties. For each \(d\), it supplies a real vector space \(\mathcal H_d\), a cone \(\mathcal X_d(P)\subseteq\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\) containing a transported law-specific direction \(x_d(P)\), a positive prediction quadratic form \(Q_{R,d}\) on that cone, and two nonnegative source-score quadratic forms \(Q_{E,d}\) and \(Q_{O,d}\), with
\[
 p_d=Q_{R,d}\{x_d(P)\},
 \qquad v_d=F_d\{x_d(P)\}, \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
 F_d(x)=\left\{\sqrt{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}+\sqrt{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}\right\}^2. \tag{5}
\]
On the bridge-differentiable submodel class of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}bridge\text{-}differentiable\text{-}submodel}\), these source scores are gradient components; outside that class, only the source-score interpretation is asserted. Set
\[
 \Lambda_-(P)=\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_+(P)=\max_{d\in\mathcal D}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_d(P)}\frac{F_d(x)}{Q_{R,d}(x)}. \tag{6}
\]
The weakest two-sided quadratic-form envelope on the chosen cones is precisely
\[
 0<\Lambda_-(P)\le\Lambda_+(P)<\infty, \tag{7}
\]
and it implies the valid, generally conservative certificate
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\le C_{\mathrm{ord}}(P)\le\frac{\Lambda_+(P)}{\Lambda_-(P)}. \tag{8}
\]

The sharp constant in (2) or (3) is not, in general, a largest generalized eigenvalue. Indeed,
\[
 F_d(x)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\left\{
 \frac{c_{E,d}Q_{E,d}(x)}{\alpha}
 +\frac{c_{O,d}Q_{O,d}(x)}{1-\alpha}\right\}, \tag{9}
\]
so the profiled numerator is generally not a quadratic form. If \(\mathcal H_d\) is finite dimensional, \(Q_{R,d}\) is positive definite, and \(\mathcal X_d(P)=\mathcal H_d\setminus\{0\}\), a largest generalized eigenvalue at a fixed \(\alpha\) gives only a one-sided full-space envelope. Selection requires both the upper and lower envelopes in (6), and equality in (8) additionally requires saturation by law-realized, raw-risk-ordered directions. Hence equality with a largest generalized eigenvalue can hold only after adding a common-space representation, a normalization of the positive lower envelope, and the required saturation; none follows from observable-law operator bijectivity or from the raw-risk ordering alone.

defs.def:bridge-differentiable-submodel:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), and write
\[
 H_d=(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X),\qquad L_d=(S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X).
\]
A regular two-source parametric submodel \(\{P_t:|t|<t_0\}\) through \(P=P_0\), with source-conditional scores \(\ell_E\) and \(\ell_O\), is called \emph{bridge-differentiable for design \(d\) at \(P\)} when the following conditions hold.  First, the source-conditional laws are dominated on a common support and the path is differentiable in quadratic mean in each source.  Second, for all sufficiently small \(|t|\), \(P_t\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and its design-\(d\) outcome bridge \(h_{d,t}\) is unique.  Third, after identifying the common \(L_2\) coordinate spaces along the dominated path, there is \(\dot h_d\in L_2(H_d\mid G=O)\) such that
\[
 \left\|\frac{h_{d,t}-h_{d,0}}{t}-\dot h_d\right\|_{L_2(P(\cdot\mid G=O))}\longrightarrow0,
\]
and the conditional bridge equation
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_t}\{Y-h_{d,t}(H_d)\mid L_d,G=O\}=0
\]
may be differentiated at \(t=0\) in \(L_2(L_d\mid G=O)\) using the conditional-score rule.  This is a restriction on submodels, not a consequence of pointwise bijectivity of \(T_d\).
defs.def:operator-comparison-handle: Use \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{comp}}\) to compare the source-score quadratic forms underlying \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)\) with the raw residual-risk quadratic form underlying \(R_d(P)\). These source-score forms have a gradient interpretation only along the bridge-differentiable paths declared for design \(d\). The exact target is a lawwise constant bounding the raw-risk selector ratio \(\rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)\); the handle does not assert that a generalized eigenvalue is sharp and does not give an unconditional gradient or causal-efficiency interpretation.
defs.def:predictive-benchmark:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), define the two generic unrestricted observational prediction risks
\[
 R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}
 \mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O],
\]
\[
 R_d^A(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(A,X,Z_{M_d})}
 \mathbb E_P[(Y-f(A,X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O].                \tag{1}
\]
Their tie-preserving population selectors and arm-normalized source-score ratios are
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d(P),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d^A(P),
\]
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.           \tag{2}
\]
Distinctly, on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\), the transported Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm population rule uses the affine-linear residual variance \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\), not either unrestricted risk.  Under \(c(M_d,n)=nC_d\), its continuous and integer criteria, selectors, and arm-normalized ratio are those in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\):
\[
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{B},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)
 =\frac{r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor}.      \tag{3}
\]
The support is mapped only to \(M_d\), and this note's role assignment remains preattached.  No equality between \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\) and \(R_d(P)\) or \(R_d^A(P)\) is imposed away from the binary centers where it is proved.  The two unrestricted-risk rules in (1)--(2) are secondary comparisons and are not attributed to a named published proxy-selection workflow.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.
defs.def:clw-linear-cost-selector:
Fix the source-faithful transported comparison from Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\): treatment is completely randomized with equal arm allocation, and the two arms have the same affine-regression residual variance.  These are restrictions on the transported comparison, not on the persistent-confounding bridge law.  Map the published support \(\mathcal I(\gamma)\) only to \(M_d\); the role assignment \(r_d\) remains preattached by this note.

Choose a finite-dimensional nonredundant affine encoding \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\), with constant and reference columns removed, and define
\[
 \xi_d=(1,X_{\mathrm{nr}}^\top,Z_{M_d}^\top)^\top,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_d\xi_d^\top\mid G=O),
 \qquad
 g_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_dY\mid G=O).                       \tag{1}
\]
The domain \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\) consists of laws \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) such that, for every \(d\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Y^2+\|\xi_d\|^2\mid G=O)<\infty,
 \qquad \det\Gamma_d(P)\ne0,                              \tag{2}
\]
and the transported balanced comparison has the arm-homoskedastic residual required by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\).  The determinant condition concerns the full Gram matrix on the nonredundant basis; no pseudoinverse is used.  Put
\[
 \beta_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)=\Gamma_d(P)^{-1}g_d(P),
 \qquad
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)=
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \{Y-\xi_d^\top\beta_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\}^2\mid G=O
 \right].                                                   \tag{3}
\]
Under the linear paired-unit cost
\[
 c(M_d,n)=nC_d,
 \qquad C_d=c_{E,d}+c_{O,d},                                \tag{4}
\]
define the continuous and exact integer criteria by
\[
 n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=\frac{B}{C_d},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{B}, \tag{5}
\]
\[
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \begin{cases}
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)/\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor>0,\\
 +\infty,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor=0.
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{6}
\]
Retain all ties in
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B). \tag{7}
\]
The continuous and exact-integer arm-normalized best-tie ratios are
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.             \tag{8}
\]
The IKM-normalized continuous and integer ratios are defined in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\).  Equations (3)--(8) transport only the population affine-linear criterion.  The exact finite-catalogue empirical affine least-squares counterpart of equation~(3.6) is defined separately in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}empirical\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\).  Nothing here attributes persistent-confounding analysis, sequential bridge-role choice, or bridge-value results to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm, and no claim concerns their approximate OGA procedure or their original randomized-trial theorem.

assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).
