defs.def:binary-witness:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant, and take the nonredundant affine encoding \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\) to be zero-dimensional. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(C_{d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi\) and \(C_{d_{\mathrm e}}=5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and define the exact center residual function
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.                  \tag{1}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\), rather than this construction, proves that the unrestricted unadjusted risk and the distinct CLW affine-linear residual both equal (1) at the symmetric centers. No such equality is imposed on perturbations in the constrained model. The named transported CLW selector compares \(C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)/B\); the two generic unrestricted-risk selectors remain separate secondary comparisons.

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\), zero-dimensional \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\), constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j).                               \tag{2}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_{\epsilon}=P_{\chi,\epsilon}\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (2).
defs.def:regular-law-class: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}\) is the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying long- and short-term consistency, observational latent exchangeability and overlap, experimental randomization and overlap, full short-term external validity, source support, the sequential-outcome restriction, and both proxy-completeness conditions for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
defs.def:predictive-benchmark:
For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), define the two generic unrestricted observational prediction risks
\[
 R_d(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(X,Z_{M_d})}
 \mathbb E_P[(Y-f(X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O],
\]
\[
 R_d^A(P)=\inf_{f\in L_2(A,X,Z_{M_d})}
 \mathbb E_P[(Y-f(A,X,Z_{M_d}))^2\mid G=O].                \tag{1}
\]
Their tie-preserving population selectors and arm-normalized source-score ratios are
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d(P),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}R_d^A(P),
\]
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{pred}}^A(P)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.           \tag{2}
\]
Distinctly, on \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\), the transported Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm population rule uses the affine-linear residual variance \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\), not either unrestricted risk.  Under \(c(M_d,n)=nC_d\), its continuous and integer criteria, selectors, and arm-normalized ratio are those in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\):
\[
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{B},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)
 =\frac{r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor}.      \tag{3}
\]
The support is mapped only to \(M_d\), and this note's role assignment remains preattached.  No equality between \(r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\) and \(R_d(P)\) or \(R_d^A(P)\) is imposed away from the binary centers where it is proved.  The two unrestricted-risk rules in (1)--(2) are secondary comparisons and are not attributed to a named published proxy-selection workflow.
defs.def:profiled-design-value: Set \(\mathcal V_d^*(P)=\inf_{0<\alpha<1}\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)\) and retain all population ties in \(D^*(P)=\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_d^*(P)\). Define \(\gamma(P)=\min_{d\notin D^*(P)}\{\mathcal V_d^*(P)-\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)\}\), with \(\gamma(P)=+\infty\) if \(D^*(P)=\mathcal D\).
defs.def:design-value-profile:
For \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\mathcal V_d(\alpha;P)=\frac{c_{E,d}V_{E,d}}{\alpha}+\frac{c_{O,d}V_{O,d}}{1-\alpha}.
\]
Set the value to \(+\infty\) outside the observable regular set.
defs.def:clw-linear-cost-selector:
Fix the source-faithful transported comparison from Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\): treatment is completely randomized with equal arm allocation, and the two arms have the same affine-regression residual variance.  These are restrictions on the transported comparison, not on the persistent-confounding bridge law.  Map the published support \(\mathcal I(\gamma)\) only to \(M_d\); the role assignment \(r_d\) remains preattached by this note.

Choose a finite-dimensional nonredundant affine encoding \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\), with constant and reference columns removed, and define
\[
 \xi_d=(1,X_{\mathrm{nr}}^\top,Z_{M_d}^\top)^\top,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_d\xi_d^\top\mid G=O),
 \qquad
 g_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_dY\mid G=O).                       \tag{1}
\]
The domain \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\) consists of laws \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) such that, for every \(d\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Y^2+\|\xi_d\|^2\mid G=O)<\infty,
 \qquad \det\Gamma_d(P)\ne0,                              \tag{2}
\]
and the transported balanced comparison has the arm-homoskedastic residual required by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\).  The determinant condition concerns the full Gram matrix on the nonredundant basis; no pseudoinverse is used.  Put
\[
 \beta_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)=\Gamma_d(P)^{-1}g_d(P),
 \qquad
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)=
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \{Y-\xi_d^\top\beta_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\}^2\mid G=O
 \right].                                                   \tag{3}
\]
Under the linear paired-unit cost
\[
 c(M_d,n)=nC_d,
 \qquad C_d=c_{E,d}+c_{O,d},                                \tag{4}
\]
define the continuous and exact integer criteria by
\[
 n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=\frac{B}{C_d},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{B}, \tag{5}
\]
\[
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \begin{cases}
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)/\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor>0,\\
 +\infty,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor=0.
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{6}
\]
Retain all ties in
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B). \tag{7}
\]
The continuous and exact-integer arm-normalized best-tie ratios are
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.             \tag{8}
\]
The IKM-normalized continuous and integer ratios are defined in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\).  Equations (3)--(8) transport only the population affine-linear criterion.  The exact finite-catalogue empirical affine least-squares counterpart of equation~(3.6) is defined separately in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}empirical\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\).  Nothing here attributes persistent-confounding analysis, sequential bridge-role choice, or bridge-value results to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm, and no claim concerns their approximate OGA procedure or their original randomized-trial theorem.
defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

node.statement:
Fix \(\chi>1\) and \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\).  The radii \(r_\epsilon\) and \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) in Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}witness\text{-}stability}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\) may be jointly decreased, without losing any of their conclusions or those of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}joint\text{-}predictive\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\), so that every law \(P\) in the resulting \(r_\epsilon\)-ball satisfies
\[
 2C_{d_{\mathrm p}}r_{d_{\mathrm p}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)
 <C_{d_{\mathrm e}}r_{d_{\mathrm e}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(P),   \tag{1}
\]
and hence, for every \(B\ge5\chi=C_{d_{\mathrm p}}\),
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=\{d_{\mathrm p}\},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P_\epsilon;B).               \tag{2}
\]
Every law in the resulting \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\)-ball also satisfies
\[
 D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)=\{d_{\mathrm e}\},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{IKM,int}}(P;B)
 =\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P;B)
 >\frac12\rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}(P_\epsilon;B) \tag{3}
\]
for every \(B\ge5\chi\).  At the center itself, (2)--(3) hold for every \(B\ge5\chi\), and both integer ratios equal their corresponding continuous center ratios.
node.justification: A budget-independent residual margin upgrades eventual floor-count agreement to exact selection for every feasible integer budget on the whole relative finite-cell neighborhood.
node.gap: The earlier stability result supplied only a law-specific eventual threshold and did not define exact-integer bridge-value ratios.
node.consumer: It is the uniform stability certificate used by the exact integer impossibility theorem and the binary-region definitions.

thm:exact-integer-clw-predictive-failure.proof_tex:
The center residual and cost formulas in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\), combined with the floor inequalities (52), give
\[
 B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm p}}^{\mathrm{int}}<3
 \le B\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d_{\mathrm e}}^{\mathrm{int}}
\]
for every \(B\ge5\chi\).  Hence the integer selector is \(\{d_{\mathrm p}\}\).  The same lemma gives \(D^*=D_{\mathrm{IKM}}^*=\{d_{\mathrm e}\}\), equality of the continuous named and unadjusted generic ratios, and formula (1).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}treatment\text{-}aware\text{-}sharp\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) adds equality of the treatment-aware ratios.  Because the integer and continuous named selectors are the same singleton, the two integer ratios equal their continuous analogues.  This proves all eight equalities.  Dropping the first nonnegative square-root term in (1) gives the stated lower bound, and expansion at fixed \(\chi\) gives (2).

Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}region}\) chooses the radii after Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}exact\text{-}integer\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\).  Hence for each center ball and every \(B\ge5\chi\), the integer ratio equals the continuous named ratio and exceeds half the corresponding center value.  Every center belongs to its ball, while the center lower bound diverges as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\); this proves the first equality in (3).  The IKM region and conclusion (3) of the stability lemma prove the second in the same way.

For every feasible pair \((\chi,B)\), the integer ratio equals \(\rho_\chi(\epsilon)\) and is independent of \(B\).  Conversely, for every \(\chi>1\), the feasible set of budgets is nonempty, for example at \(B=5\chi\).  Therefore taking the infimum over all jointly feasible pairs gives exactly
\[
 \inf_{\substack{\chi>1\\B\ge5\chi}}
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon};B)
 =\inf_{\chi>1}\rho_\chi(\epsilon),
\]
and the identical argument applies to the IKM-normalized ratio.  The rescaled optimization in the sharp-elbow lemma then gives (5) and the cube-root minimizing scale.  The final budget-schedule qualification follows because feasibility of the minimizing center is exactly \(B_\epsilon\ge5\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\).

defs.def:binary-ikmw-region:
Fix \(\chi>1\).  For every \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), jointly decrease \(r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\) as permitted by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}exact\text{-}integer\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\).  Let \(\delta_\epsilon\) be the radius in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}region}\), choose
\[
 0<\widetilde\delta_\epsilon
 <\min\{\delta_\epsilon,r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{IKM}}\},
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}^{\mathrm{IKM}}
 =\bigcup_{0<\epsilon<10^{-3}}
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi):
 \|P-P_\epsilon\|_{\mathrm{cell}}<\widetilde\delta_\epsilon\right\}. \tag{1}
\]
The radii retain the conclusions used to define \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{bin}}\), together with the strict IKM optimizer ordering and the exact-integer IKM-ratio stability from Lemmas~\(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}stability}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}exact\text{-}integer\text{-}binary\text{-}stability}\).  This is a relatively open subset of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\).

defs.def:clw-linear-cost-selector:
Fix the source-faithful transported comparison from Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\): treatment is completely randomized with equal arm allocation, and the two arms have the same affine-regression residual variance.  These are restrictions on the transported comparison, not on the persistent-confounding bridge law.  Map the published support \(\mathcal I(\gamma)\) only to \(M_d\); the role assignment \(r_d\) remains preattached by this note.

Choose a finite-dimensional nonredundant affine encoding \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\), with constant and reference columns removed, and define
\[
 \xi_d=(1,X_{\mathrm{nr}}^\top,Z_{M_d}^\top)^\top,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_d\xi_d^\top\mid G=O),
 \qquad
 g_d(P)=\mathbb E_P(\xi_dY\mid G=O).                       \tag{1}
\]
The domain \(\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{CLW}}\) consists of laws \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) such that, for every \(d\in\mathcal D\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Y^2+\|\xi_d\|^2\mid G=O)<\infty,
 \qquad \det\Gamma_d(P)\ne0,                              \tag{2}
\]
and the transported balanced comparison has the arm-homoskedastic residual required by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}clw\text{-}population\text{-}design\text{-}rule}\).  The determinant condition concerns the full Gram matrix on the nonredundant basis; no pseudoinverse is used.  Put
\[
 \beta_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)=\Gamma_d(P)^{-1}g_d(P),
 \qquad
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)=
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \{Y-\xi_d^\top\beta_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)\}^2\mid G=O
 \right].                                                   \tag{3}
\]
Under the linear paired-unit cost
\[
 c(M_d,n)=nC_d,
 \qquad C_d=c_{E,d}+c_{O,d},                                \tag{4}
\]
define the continuous and exact integer criteria by
\[
 n_{\mathrm{CLW},B}(d)=\frac{B}{C_d},
 \qquad
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)=\frac{C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)}{B}, \tag{5}
\]
\[
 \Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \begin{cases}
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)/\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor>0,\\
 +\infty,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor=0.
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{6}
\]
Retain all ties in
\[
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)
 =\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B). \tag{7}
\]
The continuous and exact-integer arm-normalized best-tie ratios are
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}(P;B)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\min_{d\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{CLW}}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)}\mathcal V_d^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)}.             \tag{8}
\]
The IKM-normalized continuous and integer ratios are defined in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ikmw\text{-}normalized\text{-}design\text{-}value}\).  Equations (3)--(8) transport only the population affine-linear criterion.  The exact finite-catalogue empirical affine least-squares counterpart of equation~(3.6) is defined separately in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}empirical\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\).  Nothing here attributes persistent-confounding analysis, sequential bridge-role choice, or bridge-value results to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm, and no claim concerns their approximate OGA procedure or their original randomized-trial theorem.

assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

node.justification: This is the exact integer-budget named headline: feasible floor counts preserve the wrong predictive choice and its unbounded bridge-value loss.
node.gap: The fixed-system bridge literature and the transported continuous CLW comparison did not give an all-feasible-budget integer theorem or the corresponding integer-selector ratios.
node.consumer: A designer can reject the affine predictive rule before purchasing units and can audit the precise budget feasibility required for the optimized elbow.

thm:empirical-clw-integer-selector.proof_tex:
Let \(m_O\) denote the number of observational pilot records.  At every center \(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m}(G=O)=1/2\), so
\[
 \frac{m_O}{m}=\frac12+O_P(m^{-1/2}),
 \qquad P(m_O<m/4)\longrightarrow0.                       \tag{53}
\]
Every coordinate product in \(Y^2\), \(\xi_dY\), or \(\xi_d\xi_d^\top\) is bounded uniformly on the binary family.  Expressing an observational average as the ratio of its \(m^{-1}\)-scaled source-weighted sum to \(m_O/m\), Chebyshev's inequality and (53) give, uniformly over the two designs and finitely many coordinates,
\[
 \max_{d\in\mathcal D}\left(
 |\widehat s_{d,m}-s_d|
 +\|\widehat g_{d,m}-g_d\|
 +\|\widehat\Gamma_{d,m}-\Gamma_d\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \right)=O_P(m^{-1/2}),                                   \tag{54}
\]
where these empirical moments are proof intermediates obtained by expanding the quadratic in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}clw\text{-}empirical\text{-}linear\text{-}cost\text{-}selector}\), and the population moments are evaluated at \(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m}\).

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\) gives Gram eigenvalues \(1,1\pm xy\).  For \(d_{\mathrm p}\), \(xy=\epsilon_my_\chi<10^{-3}\), and for \(d_{\mathrm e}\), \(xy=1/4\).  Hence
\[
 \min_{d\in\mathcal D}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma_d)\ge\frac34. \tag{55}
\]
Equations (54)--(55) imply that, with probability tending to one, every empirical Gram is nonsingular with smallest eigenvalue at least \(3/8\).  On this event,
\[
 \widehat r_{d,m}^{\mathrm{lin}}
 =\widehat s_{d,m}-\widehat g_{d,m}^\top
 \widehat\Gamma_{d,m}^{-1}\widehat g_{d,m},
 \qquad
 r_d^{\mathrm{lin}}=s_d-g_d^\top\Gamma_d^{-1}g_d.          \tag{56}
\]
The inverse identity
\[
 \widehat\Gamma_{d,m}^{-1}-\Gamma_d^{-1}
 =\widehat\Gamma_{d,m}^{-1}
 (\Gamma_d-\widehat\Gamma_{d,m})\Gamma_d^{-1}             \tag{57}
\]
and the uniform inverse bounds from (55) show that the difference in (56) is \(O_P(m^{-1/2})\), uniformly in \(d\).  On the exceptional singular event the minimized residual remains in \([0,1]\), since the zero coefficient is feasible and \(Y^2=1\); the exceptional probability tends to zero, so it does not alter the \(O_P(m^{-1/2})\) conclusion.  This proves (1).

Fix \(B\ge5\chi\).  Both floor counts are positive.  Multiplication of (1) by the fixed constants \(C_d/B\) proves the continuous criterion rate, and division by the fixed positive integers \(\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor\) proves (2).

It remains to show that the population gaps do not collapse as \(\epsilon_m\downarrow0\).  The center formulas give
\[
 C_{d_{\mathrm p}}r_{d_{\mathrm p}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})<\frac32,
 \qquad
 C_{d_{\mathrm e}}r_{d_{\mathrm e}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})=3, \tag{58}
\]
so the continuous population gap is bounded below by \(3/(2B)\).  For the integer criterion, set
\[
 k_{\mathrm p}=\left\lfloor\frac{B}{5\chi}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 k_{\mathrm e}=\left\lfloor\frac B5\right\rfloor.
\]
Both integers are positive.  If \(z=B/(5\chi)\), then \(z<2\lfloor z\rfloor=2k_{\mathrm p}\), so
\[
 k_{\mathrm e}\le\chi z<2\chi k_{\mathrm p}.
\]
Consequently the fixed number
\[
 \delta_{\chi,B}
 =\frac{3}{5k_{\mathrm e}}-
 \frac{3}{10\chi k_{\mathrm p}}>0.                        \tag{59}
\]
Since
\[
 r_{d_{\mathrm p}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})
 <\frac3{10\chi},
 \qquad
 r_{d_{\mathrm e}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})=\frac35,
\]
the exact integer criterion gap exceeds \(\delta_{\chi,B}\) for every \(m\).  The criterion consistency and the two fixed positive gaps imply
\[
 P_{\chi,\epsilon_m}\!\left\{
 \widehat d_{\mathrm{CLW},m}(B)
 =\widehat d_{\mathrm{CLW},m}^{\mathrm{int}}(B)
 =d_{\mathrm p}\right\}\longrightarrow1.                \tag{60}
\]
At \(B=5\chi\), \(k_{\mathrm p}=1\) and (59) remains strict, so the boundary is included.

On the event in (60), each achieved empirical ratio equals the corresponding population profile ratio at \(d_{\mathrm p}\).  Balanced treatment makes the IKM profile one quarter of the arm-normalized profile design by design, so the ratios agree, and the sharp-elbow lower bound gives
\[
 \frac{\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm p}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})}
 {\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})}
 =\frac{\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm p},\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})}
 {\mathcal V_{d_{\mathrm e},\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P_{\chi,\epsilon_m})}
 >\frac{\epsilon_m^{-2}+14}{726}\longrightarrow\infty.  \tag{61}
\]
For every finite threshold, (61) eventually exceeds it and the event in (60) has probability tending to one.  This proves (4).  No relation between \(m\) and \(\epsilon_m\) was used.  Each \(\epsilon_m\) is strictly positive, so every law on the path is regular; \(\epsilon=0\) is only a singular limit.  No step uses OGA or a bridge learner.

defs.def:binary-witness:
Fix an arbitrary prescribed \(\chi>1\). Set \(K=4\), \(c_1=c_2=(5\chi-3)/4\), \(c_3=c_4=1/2\), \(b_E=1\), \(b_O=2\), and \(\kappa=(5\chi-3)/2\), and put
\[
 y_{\chi}=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{10\chi}}.
\]
Let \(X\) and every \(S_{2d}\) be constant, and take the nonredundant affine encoding \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\) to be zero-dimensional. Set \(P_{\epsilon}(G=E)=P_{\epsilon}(G=O)=1/2\), and let a Rademacher \(U\) be independent of \(G\). In source \(E\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=E)=1/2\); in source \(O\), \(P_{\epsilon}(T=t\mid U=u,G=O)=(1+tu/4)/2\). The proxies \(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(U\), are independent of \(G,A\) conditional on \(U\), and form
\[
 Z(a)=(W_{\epsilon},W_{y_{\chi}},W_{1/2}^{(1)},W_{1/2}^{(2)}),
\]
while \(Y(a)=U\) for both treatments. Take \(\mathcal D=\{d_{\mathrm p},d_{\mathrm e}\}\), where \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \(W_{\epsilon}\) to role one and \(W_{y_{\chi}}\) to role three, whereas \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \(W_{1/2}^{(1)}\) to role one and \(W_{1/2}^{(2)}\) to role three. Then
\[
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi-1}{2},\qquad
 c_{O,d_{\mathrm p}}=\frac{5\chi+1}{2},\qquad
 c_{E,d_{\mathrm e}}=2,\qquad c_{O,d_{\mathrm e}}=3,
\]
so the paired costs are \(C_{d_{\mathrm p}}=5\chi\) and \(C_{d_{\mathrm e}}=5\). For a design with early signal \(x\) and late signal \(y\), the candidate bridges are
\[
 h_d(l,a)=\frac{l}{y},
 \qquad
 q_d(e,a)=\frac{1-(2a-1)e/(4x)}{1-1/16},
\]
and define the exact center residual function
\[
 R(x,y)=\frac{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}{1-x^2y^2}.                  \tag{1}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}sharp\text{-}uniform\text{-}binary\text{-}elbow}\), rather than this construction, proves that the unrestricted unadjusted risk and the distinct CLW affine-linear residual both equal (1) at the symmetric centers. No such equality is imposed on perturbations in the constrained model. The named transported CLW selector compares \(C_dr_d^{\mathrm{lin}}(P)/B\); the two generic unrestricted-risk selectors remain separate secondary comparisons.

The \emph{binary constrained finite-cell model} \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bin}}(\chi)\) is the family of laws \(P\) with the preceding prescribed catalogue, costs, cap, and role assignments, constant \(X\), zero-dimensional \(X_{\mathrm{nr}}\), constant \(S_{2d}\), latent variables \(U,T,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4\in\{-1,1\}\), \(A=(T+1)/2\), and potential variables
\[
 Z(a)=(W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4),\qquad Y(a)=U,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For strictly positive probability vectors \((\pi_g:g\in\{E,O\})\), \((\nu_u:u\in\{-1,1\})\), \((\lambda_t:t\in\{-1,1\})\), observational treatment kernels \(e_u(t)\), and proxy kernels \(k_{j,u}(w)\), its latent-cell mass factorizes as
\[
 P(G=g,U=u,T=t,W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_4=w_4)
 =\pi_g\nu_u\bigl\{\mathbf 1\{g=E\}\lambda_t
 +\mathbf 1\{g=O\}e_u(t)\bigr\}
 \prod_{j=1}^4k_{j,u}(w_j).                               \tag{2}
\]
Thus \(U\) is independent of \(G\), treatment is randomized independently of \(U\) in source \(E\), and the four proxies are mutually independent conditional on \(U\) and invariant across source and treatment. The design \(d_{\mathrm p}\) assigns \((W_1,W_2)\) to roles one and three, and \(d_{\mathrm e}\) assigns \((W_3,W_4)\) to roles one and three; role two is constant. For each \(0<\epsilon<10^{-3}\), the preceding center \(P_{\epsilon}=P_{\chi,\epsilon}\) is the point having \(\pi_E=\pi_O=1/2\), \(\nu_{-1}=\nu_1=1/2\), \(\lambda_{-1}=\lambda_1=1/2\), \(e_u(t)=(1+tu/4)/2\), and
\[
 k_{j,u}(w)=\frac{1+s_juw}{2},
 \qquad
 (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)=(\epsilon,y_{\chi},1/2,1/2).
\]
The model is parameterized by the relative interiors of these finite probability simplices. Its relative topology is equivalently the Euclidean parameter topology or the maximum-norm topology \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{cell}}\) induced by the complete latent-cell vector in (2).

Order the full-catalogue pilot records by their original indices and let
\[
 \mathcal I_{m,O}=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:G_i=O\},
 \qquad m_O=|\mathcal I_{m,O}|.
\]
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), define the exact observational-pilot affine residual quadratic
\[
 \widehat r_{d,m}^{\mathrm{lin}}=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \min_{b\in\mathbb R^{\dim(\xi_d)}}
 \frac1{m_O}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{m,O}}
 \{Y_i-\xi_{d,i}^\top b\}^2,&m_O>0,\\[6pt]
 0,&m_O=0.
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{1}
\]
This finite convex quadratic is evaluable even when its empirical Gram matrix is singular.  Define
\[
 \widehat\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d,m}(B)
 =\frac{C_d\widehat r_{d,m}^{\mathrm{lin}}}{B},
\]
\[
 \widehat\Psi_{\mathrm{CLW},d,m}^{\mathrm{int}}(B)=
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat r_{d,m}^{\mathrm{lin}}/\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor,
 &\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor>0,\\
 +\infty,&\lfloor B/C_d\rfloor=0.
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{2}
\]
Let \(\widehat d_{\mathrm{CLW},m}(B)\) and
\(\widehat d_{\mathrm{CLW},m}^{\mathrm{int}}(B)\) be the deterministically tie-broken minimizers of the two criteria in (2) over \(\mathcal D\).  Their exact-integer achieved ratios are
\[
 \widehat\rho_{\mathrm{CLW},m}^{\mathrm{int}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\mathcal V_{\widehat d_{\mathrm{CLW},m}^{\mathrm{int}}(B)}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d'}^*(P)},
\]
\[
 \widehat\rho_{\mathrm{CLW},m}^{\mathrm{IKM,int}}(P;B)=
 \frac{\mathcal V_{\widehat d_{\mathrm{CLW},m}^{\mathrm{int}}(B),\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}
 {\min_{d'\in\mathcal D}\mathcal V_{d',\mathrm{IKM}}^*(P)}. \tag{3}
\]
This is the exact finite-catalogue affine least-squares minimizer corresponding to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm equation~(3.6), transported with support mapped only to \(M_d\).  It does not implement or analyze approximate OGA.
defs.def:common-identification-class:
\[
\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{id}}
=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}:\theta_d(P)=\tau\text{ for every }d\in\mathcal D\}.
\]

assumptions.ass:independent-pilot: \(\mathcal P_m\) is independent of the main-study observations used to construct \(\widehat\tau_B\).
assumptions.ass:source-support: \(p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=E)/p_P(U,X\mid A=a,G=O)<\infty\) almost surely for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:sequential-outcomes: \((Y(a),S_{3d}(a))\perp S_{1d}(a)\mid S_{2d}(a),U,X,G=O\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).
assumptions.ass:late-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{3d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:early-proxy-completeness: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and square-integrable \(v\), \(\mathbb E_P[v(U)\mid S_{1d},S_{2d},A=a,X,G=O]=0\) almost surely implies \(v(U)=0\) almost surely.
assumptions.ass:observed-outcome-bridge-existence:
For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(h_d\) is a square-integrable solution of
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O]
=\mathbb E_P[h_d(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\mid S_{2d},S_{1d},A,X,G=O].
\]
assumptions.ass:selection-bridge-existence: For every \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(q_d\) is a square-integrable solution of \(p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=E)/p_P(S_{3d},S_{2d},X\mid A,G=O)=(T_d^\star q_d)(S_{3d},S_{2d},A,X)\).

node.justification: A feasible pilot OLS implementation consistently optimizes the affine criterion yet inherits its divergent bridge-value loss.
node.gap: This covers the exact finite-catalogue empirical minimizer corresponding to CLW equation~(3.6), not approximate OGA or a growing-model learner.
node.consumer: It rules out population-oracle infeasibility as an explanation for the negative design result.

oeq:finite-predictive-guarantee.source_fingerprint: {"kind":"openendedquestion","statement":"Using \\(\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{comp}}\\), characterize the weakest law-primitive comparison of the design-specific operators \\(T_d\\), the cost-aware objectives \\(\\Psi_{\\mathrm{CLW},d}(P;B)\\), and the two source-gradient quadratic forms that implies a finite constant \\(C(P)<\\infty\\) with \\(\\rho_{\\mathrm{pred}}(P)\\le C(P)\\), and determine whether the sharp constant is the largest generalized eigenvalue of the transported cost-weighted quadratic-form pair.","depends_on":["def:operator-comparison-handle","def:predictive-benchmark"]}

prose_overlay.tldr: Long-term data fusion requires choosing which short-term outcomes to measure, assigning their sequential proxy roles, and allocating a fixed budget between randomized short-term units and observational long-term follow-up.  This note makes that measurement design the argument of the two-source bridge score profile.  For the source-faithful Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm affine-linear specialization, an explicit regular two-design family shows that the exact integer-budget population rule selects \(d_{\mathrm p}\) for every \(B\ge5\chi\), while both the arm-normalized and IKM-normalized bridge profiles select \(d_{\mathrm e}\).  The corresponding integer-selector ratios are unbounded on relatively open common-identification regions; at fixed \(\chi\) their center ratio has leading coefficient \((5\chi+1)/\{363(10\chi-3)\}\), and optimization over jointly feasible \((\chi,B)\) gives the sharp \(1/726\) elbow and cube-root cost scale.  An exact finite-catalogue pilot OLS minimizer corresponding to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm equation~(3.6) is root-\(m\) risk consistent yet selects the same inefficient design along the binary triangular path.  The positive prescription is to enumerate the observable bridge design value from a full-catalogue pilot, use the profiled square-root source allocation, and conduct selected-design-only Wald inference under the declared learner and variance conditions.
prose_overlay.related_work: ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 supplies the persistent-confounding bridge model, the fixed-system source-score limit law, and the local efficiency theorem under its identification, uniqueness, bijectivity, and fixed-ratio premises.  This note treats the measured subset, sequential role assignment, and source allocation as design arguments selected by an independent pilot, and invokes absolute causal efficiency only through the separately cited fixed-system result.  CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020, Section~3.2, Assumption~3.1, Lemma~3.1, and equations~(3.3)--(3.6), supplies the balanced-treatment affine-linear residual-variance-over-sample-size criterion and its pre-experimental empirical least-squares counterpart.  The present transport maps support only to \(M_d\), keeps bridge roles preattached, uses linear paired-unit costs and exact floor counts, and analyzes the exact finite-catalogue OLS minimizer corresponding to equation~(3.6); it does not evaluate the original randomized-trial theorem or approximate OGA and does not attribute persistent-confounding analysis or bridge-role choice to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm.  KallusMao2025 compares efficiency with and without a fixed surrogate vector rather than optimizing a costly subset-role system.  TaoZengLin2020 and WangWangMiao2023 optimize two-phase sampling for fixed measured variables or a fixed full-data influence-function setting, whereas this note selects proxy subset, sequential role assignment, and source allocation.  GuptaLiptonChilders2024 learns allocations for a supplied moment system.  BennettKallusMaoNeweySyrgkanisUehara2023 studies inference on strongly identified functionals of weakly identified nuisances, and ZhangLiMiaoTchetgenTchetgen2023 develops proximal inference without bridge uniqueness; this note instead maintains unique bridges, bijective operators, and explicit weak--strong learner rates and claims neither weak-identification nor nonuniqueness robustness.  ChernozhukovEtAl2018 supplies cross-fitting and orthogonal product-rate machinery, while the present inference contribution is independent-pilot design and allocation selection, selected-design-only fitting, and conditional random-index Wald inference.  YangEcklesDhillonAral2024 and LalImbensHull2026 are contextual comparisons about predictive and causal relevance, and MareisDrton2026 treats cost-aware staged measurement in a linear front-door model rather than the two-bridge long-term fusion problem.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The named conclusion is confined to the source-faithful affine-linear CLW specialization, its exact floor-budget population rule, and the exact finite-catalogue OLS minimizer corresponding to equation~(3.6).  It does not analyze approximate OGA, arbitrary predictive algorithms, the original randomized-trial theorem, bridge-role choice, or persistent-confounding analysis by Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm.  Equality between the affine residual and unrestricted \(R_d(P)\) is proved only at the symmetric centers.  The witness region is relatively open only inside the constrained finite-cell model, and the inverse-bridge envelope is deliberately nonuniform as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\).  At one fixed finite budget the feasible integer centers obey \(\chi\le B/5\); the cube-root \(1/726\) optimization therefore requires joint budget feasibility or a growing budget schedule.  Post-selection inference remains conditional on the declared selected-path learner, multiplier, product-rate, pilot-variance, and main-study variance conditions outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: For every fixed \(\chi>1\), the paper proves that the named exact integer population selector chooses \(d_{\mathrm p}\) at the centers and throughout suitably shrunk constrained-model neighborhoods for every \(B\ge5\chi\).  Its arm-normalized and IKM-normalized integer-selector ratios equal the corresponding continuous center ratios, have fixed-\(\chi\) leading coefficient \((5\chi+1)/\{363(10\chi-3)\}>1/726\), and remain unbounded on the relatively open regions.  The value \(1/726\) arises after optimization over jointly feasible \((\chi,B)\), with \(\chi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\epsilon)\sim\sqrt[3]{18}\epsilon^{-2/3}/15\) and the stated second-order term; it is not an unrestricted fixed-finite-budget optimization over \(\chi\).  Along the bounded finite-cell path with uniformly nonsingular full Grams, the independently funded pilot OLS criterion is uniformly root-\(m\) consistent and its exact integer selector inherits the divergent ratio without any rate link between \(m\) and \(\epsilon_m\).  Generic unrestricted \(R_d(P)\) and \(R_d^A(P)\) results are secondary and remain distinct from affine linear risk off center.  The proposed positive rule enumerates observable bridge values; Wald inference targets the selected observed bridge contrast on the observable class and the causal long-term effect only on the common-identification subclass.  Absolute IKM efficiency and broader learner attainability retain their separately stated premises.  OPEN (maintained condition ass:uniform-outcome-weak-rate): broader primitive learner attainability remains outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass OPEN (maintained condition ass:uniform-outcome-strong-rate): broader primitive learner attainability remains outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass OPEN (maintained condition ass:uniform-selection-weak-rate): broader primitive learner attainability remains outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass OPEN (maintained condition ass:uniform-selection-strong-rate): broader primitive learner attainability remains outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass OPEN (maintained condition ass:uniform-bridge-product-rate): broader primitive learner attainability remains outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass OPEN (maintained condition ass:postselection-multiplier-condition): broader primitive learner attainability remains outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass OPEN (maintained condition ass:pilot-gradient-variance-rate): broader primitive learner attainability remains outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass OPEN (maintained condition ass:main-gradient-variance-rate): broader primitive learner attainability remains outside the proved fixed-dimensional subclass

project_justification.gap: The long-term bridge and surrogate-efficiency literatures treat the measured proxy system and source ratio as fixed.  Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm optimize affine predictive residual variance and sample size in a randomized-trial collection problem, but neither that work nor the fixed-system bridge literature supplies an efficiency guarantee for transporting this objective to costly sequential proxy designs, an exact integer-budget comparison, or an analysis of its finite-catalogue empirical least-squares minimizer under persistent confounding.
project_justification.niche: A finite costed catalogue with preattached sequential roles creates nonnested inverse problems with separate experimental and observational information bottlenecks.  Exact floor counts and a feasible pilot selector make it possible to distinguish failure of the affine predictive objective from identification failure or population-oracle infeasibility.
project_justification.fill: The note gives a source-faithful nonredundant full-Gram transport of the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm affine-linear criterion, proves its continuous and exact integer-budget rules, and constructs a regular common-identification region on which every \(B\ge5\chi\) selects the wrong bridge design with unbounded arm-normalized and IKM ratios.  It carries the exact center formula to the integer ratios, separates the fixed-\(\chi\) coefficient from the jointly feasible optimized \(1/726\) elbow, and proves that the exact finite-catalogue pilot OLS minimizer corresponding to equation~(3.6) is root-\(m\) consistent but inherits the divergent ratio.  Generic unrestricted-risk selectors remain secondary comparisons; bridge-value enumeration, source allocation, and conditional post-selection Wald inference provide the positive design rule.

sampling_model.design: An independent full-catalogue pilot supports two distinct measurable rules: the proposed bridge-value selector fits both bridges and their source-score variances for every admissible design, whereas the Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm comparator computes each design's observational affine OLS residual and divides it by the continuous or exact floor-budget count.  The proposed rule fixes \(\widehat d_m\), its square-root budget share, and the integer experimental and follow-up counts; the independent main study then measures only the selected catalogue subset in both sources and observes \(Y\) only in observational follow-up.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The general Wald theorem is conditional on the declared selected-path weak and strong bridge rates, weak--strong product rate, multiplier condition, and pilot and main-study score-variance rates. The fixed-dimensional attainability theorem verifies these conditions for known bounded finite-dimensional bridge and test bases, uniformly nonsingular moment matrices, bounded basis Gram spectra, source-arm positivity, and a \((4+\delta)\)-moment for \(Y\). It obtains all four bridge rates at \(B^{-1/2}\), the multiplier rate at \(B^{-1/2}\), pilot variance error \(m^{-1/2}\), and main-study variance error \(B^{-1/2}\).
sampling_model.overlap: The observable theorem assumes source-arm positivity directly. Latent observational overlap, experimental randomization, source support, external validity, and completeness belong only to the stronger causal class and are not used by the selected-contrast limit law.
sampling_model.units: Within the pilot and within the main study, the experimental and observational source samples are mutually independent and consist of independent and identically distributed observations from their respective source-conditional laws. Pilot source-arm sizes, main-study source-arm sizes, and fixed-fold training and evaluation sizes are proportional to \(m\) or \(B\) on the fixed-dimensional attainability subclass.

lem:designwise-gradient.justification: The repaired lemma identifies the observed bridge contrast law-by-law and derives its two source gradient components only along the declared bridge-differentiable regular submodels.  The restriction is placed exactly at the load-bearing differentiation of the conditional bridge equation.
lem:designwise-gradient.gap: Pointwise \(L_2\) bridge existence and bijectivity do not supply local inverse continuity or differentiability of the bridge solution along every regular path.
lem:designwise-gradient.consumer: A downstream designer may always use \(V_{E,d}\) and \(V_{O,d}\) as source-score variance inputs, and may call their combination a gradient variance only after verifying bridge-differentiability for the relevant submodel class.

thm:budget-profile.justification: Profiles the exact two-source source-score variance under monetary costs and quantifies integer-count rounding.
thm:budget-profile.gap: The anchor fixes a limiting source ratio; this algebraic profile optimizes it under design-specific costs, while the cross-design advance comes from comparing admissible measurement systems rather than from claiming a new fixed-system efficiency formula.
thm:budget-profile.consumer: A study designer receives an explicit budget share and profiled source-score value, with causal-efficiency interpretation only under separately stated canonical-gradient premises.

thm:predictive-impossibility-unequal-cos.justification: The canonical witness now makes the prediction-selected design strictly more expensive and proves divergence on an open range of cost vectors.
thm:predictive-impossibility-unequal-cos.gap: No cited measurement-design result covers a nonparametric two-bridge persistent-confounding model or proves an unequal-cost prediction-to-efficiency impossibility.
thm:predictive-impossibility-unequal-cos.consumer: Organizations can no longer dismiss the obstruction as an equal-cost artifact or an identification failure.

thm:finite-catalogue-predictive-guarante.justification: The theorem distinguishes exact fixed-law enumeration from a uniform guarantee. Its two-rule companion supplies the treatment-aware and IKM-normalized enumerations.
thm:finite-catalogue-predictive-guarante.gap: Finiteness of the catalogue guarantees evaluability at a fixed law but no law-uniform approximation factor for either prediction ordering.
thm:finite-catalogue-predictive-guarante.consumer: It gives downstream readers the exact constants to compute and the condition whose uniform boundedness would be needed on a restricted law class.

thm:pilot-oracle-regret.justification: The generic regret certificate is operational under the fixed-dimensional lemma, which supplies uniform pilot source-score variance error of order \(m^{-1/2}\).
thm:pilot-oracle-regret.gap: Outside the fixed-dimensional regime the displayed pilot variance condition remains a hypothesis, not a consequence of the observable class.
thm:pilot-oracle-regret.consumer: A pilot designer with fixed known bridge bases obtains a feasible plug-in selector with the theorem's oracle-regret bound.

thm:postselection-wald.justification: Transfers a deterministic-path orthogonal expansion through an independent pilot-selected finite design and allocation, using only the selected main-study fits and a totalized variance estimator.
thm:postselection-wald.gap: Imbens--Kallus--Mao--Wang fix the proxy system and source ratio; Bennett et al. and Zhang et al. address weak or nonunique bridge settings; Chernozhukov et al. supply cross-fitting. This theorem instead conditions on unique bridges and explicit learner rates and transfers inference through an independent-pilot random finite design and allocation.
thm:postselection-wald.consumer: A downstream analyst obtains a Gaussian statistic and Wald interval for the selected observed bridge contrast, and for the causal effect on the common-identification subclass.

lem:second-order-allocation-loss.justification: The explicit finite-family expansion shows that estimating the square-root allocation changes the profiled value only quadratically, apart from integer rounding.
lem:second-order-allocation-loss.consumer: The pilot designer can separate first-order measurement-system regret from second-order allocation error.
lem:second-order-allocation-loss.gap: The fixed-ratio anchor does not quantify the cost of learning the source allocation from a pilot.

thm:predictive-impossibility.justification: The named CLW specialization selects a predictively attractive but bridge-inefficient proxy design, with exact cost and ratio formulas.
thm:predictive-impossibility.gap: Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm do not analyze persistent-confounding bridges; the transport maps only measured support and retains their affine criterion.
thm:predictive-impossibility.consumer: A measurement designer should compare bridge-value gaps instead of using affine residual fit as an information surrogate.

lem:binary-witness-stability.justification: Continuity on the constrained finite-cell model turns the center separation into a relatively open regular common-identification obstruction.
lem:binary-witness-stability.gap: The stability is relative to the factorized finite-cell model and does not assert ambient-simplex openness.
lem:binary-witness-stability.consumer: It certifies that the failure is not confined to an isolated law.

lem:ikmw-fixed-design-limit.justification: This is a source-faithful comparison node that binds the artificial-superpopulation norm and preserves the source's printed score normalization.
lem:ikmw-fixed-design-limit.gap: It does not prove the arm-normalized expansion used by this note and is not a substitute for that derivation.
lem:ikmw-fixed-design-limit.consumer: Readers can audit exactly what is imported from the fixed-system paper and what is newly proved here.

lem:binary-regular-locus-relatively-open.justification: The lemma proves that a genuine relative ball in the named finite-cell model lies inside the regular class; bridge existence at nearby laws is constructed by invertible binary channels rather than copied from the center formula.
lem:binary-regular-locus-relatively-open.gap: Regularity of an isolated witness would not establish a nondegenerate failure region.
lem:binary-regular-locus-relatively-open.consumer: The headline can attribute the predictive failure to efficiency geometry rather than identification breakdown or a knife-edge law.

lem:ikmw-fixed-system-efficiency.justification: This cited leaf records the published IKM-normalized fixed-ratio efficiency and attainment result, including its explicit \(\lambda\)-dependent variance.
lem:ikmw-fixed-system-efficiency.gap: The source establishes efficiency for the assembled two-source influence function; it does not make the two conditional source terms separate canonical gradients or justify arbitrary source-ratio sequences.
lem:ikmw-fixed-system-efficiency.consumer: The binary calculation and every absolute causal-efficiency interpretation use this leaf only after proving the normalization and all causal-identification premises.

prop:anchor-reduction.justification: Places the design calculation on the observable bridge model and reserves causal interpretation for the separate common-identification subclass.
prop:anchor-reduction.gap: The anchor fixes the short-term system and source ratio and does not optimize the finite catalogue under costs.
prop:anchor-reduction.consumer: Investigators can compare admissible measurement systems and allocate the main-study budget using source-specific gradient moments.

lem:binary-ikmw-normalized-stability.justification: Balanced treatment multiplies both source moments by one quarter, so profiling multiplies every center design value by one quarter and leaves every named or generic best-tie ratio with the same selected singleton unchanged.
lem:binary-ikmw-normalized-stability.gap: The IKM-normalized profile has an absolute causal-efficiency interpretation only under the separately cited fixed-system premises.
lem:binary-ikmw-normalized-stability.consumer: The lemma supplies the IKM stability radius used by the named and generic open-region impossibility claims.

lem:sharp-uniform-binary-elbow.justification: The full-Gram center calculation supplies the exact affine residual, bridge-score values, selector ratio, fixed-\(\chi\) coefficient, and optimized elbow inherited by the continuous and integer results.
lem:sharp-uniform-binary-elbow.gap: The calculation keeps the CLW affine residual distinct from unrestricted prediction risk away from the symmetric centers.
lem:sharp-uniform-binary-elbow.consumer: The exact formulas let a designer audit which proxy signal drives predictive fit and which drives the bridge correction.

lem:exact-allocation-curvature-floor.justification: The profiled criterion admits an exact quadratic-over-interior curvature identity, and reciprocal flooring adds a separately identified nonnegative remainder with an explicit strict bound whenever both continuous counts exceed one.
lem:exact-allocation-curvature-floor.gap: This replaces a rate-only allocation argument by an exact finite-budget decomposition while preserving the second-order \(O_P(r_{V,m}^2+B^{-1})\) consequence in its consuming results.
lem:exact-allocation-curvature-floor.consumer: Provides the shared deterministic algebra for the pilot allocation-loss lemma and oracle-regret theorem.

thm:sharp-predictive-operator-certificat.justification: Gives exact finite-catalogue constants for raw-risk ordering and separates them from conservative quadratic-form envelopes.
thm:sharp-predictive-operator-certificat.gap: A generalized eigenvalue is neither automatically sharp nor sufficient after budget profiling.
thm:sharp-predictive-operator-certificat.consumer: Analysts can compute exact lawwise constants by finite enumeration and audit any proposed operator envelope.

lem:bridge-contrast-not-ate.justification: Isolates the exact causal-equality failure formerly embedded in the gradient lemma.
lem:bridge-contrast-not-ate.gap: Completeness for functions of the latent variable alone does not eliminate discrepancies that also depend on the middle outcome.
lem:bridge-contrast-not-ate.consumer: Readers can see precisely why selected-contrast inference needs a separate causal corollary.

prop:postselection-wald-ate-corollary.justification: The corollary translates selected-contrast inference to ATE inference exactly on the common-identification class and inherits every maintained condition of the parent Wald theorem.
prop:postselection-wald-ate-corollary.gap: The equality \(\theta_d(P)=\tau\) is not available on the whole observable or causal regular class.
prop:postselection-wald-ate-corollary.consumer: Causal analysts obtain the exact additional identification restriction required for ATE coverage, without changing the selected estimator or studentizer.

lem:finite-dimensional-bridge-rates.justification: The lemma supplies the concrete non-growing-basis construction requested for primitive attainability and derives all eight rate requirements.
lem:finite-dimensional-bridge-rates.gap: The observable class alone supplies neither a learner nor inverse stability; fixed bases and uniformly nonsingular moment matrices close that gap on an explicit regime.
lem:finite-dimensional-bridge-rates.consumer: The pilot and post-selection results can use the root-sample-size rates as a verified primitive corollary.

thm:finite-dimensional-selected-path-att.justification: Provides a primitive bounded finite-dimensional regime in which every maintained bridge, product, multiplier, and variance-rate condition used downstream is derived rather than assumed.
thm:finite-dimensional-selected-path-att.gap: The repaired statement now explicitly requires pilot--main independence, mutually independent sources, and independent and identically distributed observations within each source; the proof retains the full three-term experimental centering error.
thm:finite-dimensional-selected-path-att.consumer: An analyst using bounded fixed bridge bases and uniformly nonsingular moments can invoke the pilot-regret and selected-design Wald theorems with root-sample-size rates.

thm:empirical-treatment-aware-predictive.justification: A feasible split-sample saturated predictor attains the secondary treatment-aware population choice along the binary sequence and inherits its diverging bridge-value ratio.
thm:empirical-treatment-aware-predictive.gap: This remains a secondary saturated finite-cell implementation of generic treatment-aware risk, distinct from the separately proved exact CLW equation~(3.6) affine OLS selector.
thm:empirical-treatment-aware-predictive.consumer: It shows that the secondary population obstruction is not an artifact of an infeasible oracle selector.

thm:treatment-aware-predictive-operator-.justification: This theorem gives the exact order-restricted constant for treatment-aware prediction and the valid two-sided quadratic-form certificate for the arm-normalized profile.
thm:treatment-aware-predictive-operator-.gap: A largest generalized eigenvalue is insufficient because design profiling is nonquadratic and selection requires a positive lower envelope plus saturation.
thm:treatment-aware-predictive-operator-.consumer: It characterizes precisely what additional law-class comparison would be required to rescue a finite treatment-aware prediction guarantee.

thm:two-rule-predictive-impossibility.justification: The named affine-linear obstruction and two secondary unrestricted-risk obstructions share one explicit binary mechanism and sharp center envelope.
thm:two-rule-predictive-impossibility.gap: The unrestricted rules are generic secondary comparisons and are not attributed to Carneiro--Lee--Wilhelm or arbitrary predictive procedures.
thm:two-rule-predictive-impossibility.consumer: The result separates failure of the named affine criterion from the broader lesson that outcome fit can miss inverse-bridge stability.

thm:two-rule-finite-catalogue-predictive.justification: Finite enumeration gives exact lawwise selector constants for continuous and integer named rules and both secondary risk selectors.
thm:two-rule-finite-catalogue-predictive.gap: Lawwise computability does not imply a law-uniform bridge-value guarantee.
thm:two-rule-finite-catalogue-predictive.consumer: A designer can enumerate every criterion, best-tie ratio, and pairwise order certificate in quadratic catalogue time.

thm:exact-integer-clw-predictive-failure.justification: The all-feasible-budget floor comparison is the exact named population measurement-design headline.
thm:exact-integer-clw-predictive-failure.gap: Continuous profiling alone does not certify the purchased integer design, and fixed-budget optimization cannot range over infeasible cost factors.
thm:exact-integer-clw-predictive-failure.consumer: A designer obtains a budget-feasible obstruction and an explicit certificate for when the sharp optimized elbow applies.

thm:empirical-clw-integer-selector.justification: A feasible exact finite-catalogue pilot OLS rule consistently optimizes the affine criterion yet inherits the divergent bridge-value ratio.
thm:empirical-clw-integer-selector.gap: This analyzes the exact equation-(3.6) minimizer, not approximate OGA or the original randomized-trial theorem.
thm:empirical-clw-integer-selector.consumer: It shows that population-oracle infeasibility is not the source of the negative result.

prose_overlay.interpretation: The actionable selection criterion is the pairwise bridge design-value gap \(\Delta_P(d,d')\), computed from the two source-score variances and known costs.  At the binary centers, the late proxy lets the CLW affine regression predict \(Y\) very well, but the weak early proxy makes the observational selection bridge unstable.  The exact integer rule and its empirically consistent OLS implementation therefore optimize the wrong information geometry: estimating the predictive objective accurately does not control bridge-value loss.  Every candidate remains regular and identifies the same effect on the witness region, so the obstruction is efficiency rather than identification.
